classification_rationale: Selected at Track A step 1 as the 'M full-semantic-review candidate' based on a cheap, mechanical selection-time proxy (no override link + zero enumerated <code> terms in L1). On full reading of the requirement text and its context bundle, that proxy turns out NOT to predict the true classification well: there IS a nameable deterministic trigger (arithmetic inside `unchecked {}` blocks, arithmetic in code compiled <0.8.0, or arithmetic in inline assembly -- all three are syntactically detectable via Slither/AST), so this is not text-blind FULL_SEMANTIC_REVIEW. This is EXACTLY the kind of DETERMINISTIC_TRIGGER_SEMANTIC_CONDITION / FULL_SEMANTIC_REVIEW boundary case the plan anticipated and said to record with rationale rather than resolve by fiat -- so it is recorded as such, not silently reclassified to make the selection proxy look more accurate than it was.
trigger_precision_note: Unlike req-2-verify-exact-balance-check's narrow trigger, THIS trigger is comparatively COARSE: 'presence of an unchecked{} block / pre-0.8.0 arithmetic / assembly arithmetic' does not by itself mean the arithmetic CAN actually overflow or underflow -- e.g. `unchecked { i++; }` inside a loop already bounded by a small fixed limit cannot overflow in practice, and would be a false positive if the trigger alone were treated as sufficient evidence of applicability. Determining whether overflow/underflow is ACTUALLY reachable given the code's value ranges is itself a semantic/range-analysis question, not a purely syntactic one -- meaning the semantic reviewer's job here is heavier than in req-2-verify-exact-balance-check's case: it must independently judge (a) whether the flagged arithmetic can realistically overflow/underflow given context, in addition to (b) whether a 'demonstrated need' and 'adequate guards' (the requirement's own named exception condition) are present. This blurs the line between 'trigger' and 'semantic condition' more than the balance-check requirement does -- worth treating this variation as a genuine, reportable finding about the SHAPE of DETERMINISTIC_TRIGGER_SEMANTIC_CONDITION cases, not glossing over it as a clean uniform category.

components.note: Would flag: (a) any `unchecked {}` block containing +/-/* on an integer type, (b) any arithmetic in a contract compiled at solc <0.8.0 outside a SafeMath-style wrapper, (c) any arithmetic performed via inline assembly opcodes (add/sub/mul without explicit overflow checks). Deliberately over-inclusive per the trigger_precision_note above -- this is evidence collection, not a conformance verdict; the false-positive risk noted above is exactly why judgment_authority is DETERMINISTIC_EVIDENCE_ONLY, not DETERMINISTIC_COMPLETE.

Must independently assess BOTH whether the flagged arithmetic site can realistically overflow/underflow given surrounding value constraints, AND (only if so) whether a demonstrated need plus adequate guards -- consistent with the contract author's own claims -- are present, per the requirement's own inline exception text (see context bundle: 'there is a demonstrated need ... and there are guards ... to ensure behavior consistent with the claims of the contract author'). Depends on the L8 shared LLM Judgment Layer, not yet built.

aggregation_rule: applicability_state = APPLICABLE iff trigger-unprotected-arithmetic-context fires at least once; conformance_state = semantic-review-overflow-risk-and-guards's decision when applicable, NOT_APPLICABLE otherwise.
